title: Exact singleton evaluation and K-injective Galois section model
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $k^s/k$ a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure], $s=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $\bar s=\operatorname{Spec}k^s$, and $G=\operatorname{Aut}_k(k^s)$ with its Krull topology. Use small sites in the compatible universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For a profinite set $P$ put $T[P]=\varprojlim_i\coprod_{P_i}T$ over its finite quotients [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-test-object-functor].

Let $R$ be any commutative condensed ring, $R_T=p_T^*R$, and use internal modules and ordinary unbounded derived categories [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, sk-def-sfb-module-objects, sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Write $\mathcal M_R$ for internal condensed $R$-modules and $\mathcal A_G(R)$ for such modules with an $R$-linear action of the condensed group $\underline G(P)=C(P,G)$ [def-sfb-condensed-action-module].

Let $a:X\to s$ be qcqs and let $E_R$, $F_R=E_Ra_*$, and $\Gamma_G:\mathcal A_G(R)\to\mathcal M_R$ be the normalized equivalence, geometric section functor, and invariant-submodule right adjoint of [lem-sfb-geometric-sections-adjunction]. Let $\operatorname{ev}_*:\mathcal M_R\to\mathbf{Ab}$ be evaluation at the singleton followed by forgetting scalars. Write $C(H)$ for termwise application of an additive functor $H$ to cochain complexes, $Q$ for localization at quasi-isomorphisms, and $\Gamma_X$ for global sections of $R_X$-modules followed by forgetting scalars [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology]. A complex is K-injective if every chain map from an acyclic complex to it is null-homotopic.

The functor $\operatorname{ev}_*$ is exact. Restriction to $X^s$, with invariant codomain, defines a natural isomorphism of additive functors $\gamma:\Gamma_X\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{ev}_*\Gamma_GF_R$ whose inverse is unique sheaf gluing. The left adjoint $a^*E_R^{-1}$ of $F_R$ is exact for every commutative condensed $R$, and both $C(F_R)$ and $C(\Gamma_G)$ carry K-injective complexes to K-injective complexes. The categories $\operatorname{Mod}_{R_X}$, $\mathcal M_R$ and $\mathcal A_G(R)$ have K-injective resolutions of all unbounded complexes, so the ordinary total right derived functors $\mathbf RF_R:D(R_X)\to D(\mathcal A_G(R))$ and $\mathbf R\Gamma_G:D(\mathcal A_G(R))\to D(\mathcal M_R)$ exist on all unbounded complexes [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories]. Consequently every unbounded $R_X$-complex $M$ admits a K-injective resolution $M\to I$ for which $C(F_R)I$ represents $\mathbf RF_R(M)$ and $C(\Gamma_G)C(F_R)I$ represents $(\mathbf R\Gamma_G)(\mathbf RF_R(M))$. In these coordinates the normalized derived section comparison is represented by the chain isomorphism
$$C(\gamma)_I:C(\Gamma_X)I\xrightarrow{\sim}C(\operatorname{ev}_*)C(\Gamma_G)C(F_R)I.$$
Its class is natural under the canonical changes of K-injective resolution and is the canonical derived adjunction-composition comparison, with the specified underived units and counits. No boundedness or finite cohomological dimension of $G$ is required.

proof.text: Use the internal/section-ring module equivalence of [def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. Kernels are sectionwise and cokernels are sheafified sectionwise cokernels by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]; the identical constructions on underlying abelian sheaves show that forgetting the module structure preserves kernels and cokernels. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-site-abelian-sheaf-epi-locally-surjective] gives local lifts for every module epimorphism. A covering sieve of $*$ contains a finite jointly surjective family by [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. Some member $P\to *$ is nonempty; any point of $P$ gives a continuous section $*\to P$. Restricting a local lift along this section gives a lift over $*$. Evaluation preserves kernels by their sectionwise formula and preserves epimorphisms by this argument, hence preserves short exact sequences. Forgetting the resulting $R(*)$-module structure preserves their exactness as abelian groups. This proves exactness of $\operatorname{ev}_*$ for arbitrary $R$.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, p.28; explicit splitting argument at the singleton, using sites-modules.tex Tags 03DA/03CN

proof.text: Apply the normalized right-adjoint comparison in [lem-sfb-field-action-topos-coefficients] to the underlying sheaf of $N=a_*M$, and use its ring comparison and [lem-sfb-geometric-sections-adjunction] to retain the module structures. At $P=*$ it identifies $N(s)$ with the fully fixed sections of $(E_RN)(*)$. By [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback] the underlying sheaf of $N$ is $a^{\mathrm{Ab}}_*M$, and by [def-sfb-finite-lower-star] $N(V)=M(X\times_sV)$ with restriction maps those of $M$; as $s[*]=s$ and $\Gamma_X=\operatorname{Hom}(R_X,-)$ is evaluation on the final object $X$ [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology], $N(s)=\Gamma(X,M)$ and $N(s)\to N(\bar s)$ is restriction $M(X)\to M(X^s)$. The normalized section formula identifies $(E_RN)(*)=\Gamma(X^s,M|_{X^s})$, with the specified condensed action, so the inclusion is exactly restriction to $X^s$. The equalizer comparison supplies its inverse by unique gluing. It tests invariance after every profinite base change, rather than only under individual elements of $G$. These identifications commute with module morphisms; restriction and gluing are additive. They therefore give precisely the asserted natural additive isomorphism $\gamma$.

source.place: Examples 4.1.9-4.1.10, pp.27-28; normalized ringed descent through the two cited inputs

proof.text: By [det-prop-sfb-module-pullback-exact-main], $a^*$ is exact for any commutative condensed $R$. The additive equivalence $E_R$ and its inverse are exact, and [lem-sfb-geometric-sections-adjunction] specifies $a^*E_R^{-1}\dashv F_R$; hence this left adjoint is exact. The same node specifies exact trivial inflation $T_G:\mathcal M_R\to\mathcal A_G(R)$ with right adjoint $\Gamma_G$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] to each of these two additive adjunctions. This proves K-injective preservation by $C(F_R)$ and $C(\Gamma_G)$.

source.place: Tag 08BJ, lemma-adjoint-preserve-K-injectives; exact module inverse image from the cited general coefficient result

proof.text: The three categories in the assertion are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-sfb-geometric-sections-adjunction]. Apply [lem-sfb-grothendieck-k-injective] in each, in the fixed compatible universes. For every additive $H$ used here, $Q C(H)$ on the homotopy category is triangulated: applying $H$ to a homotopy applies it to its defining additive identity, and $H$ preserves the finite biproducts and signed differential matrices defining shifts and cones. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived] gives the ordinary total right derived functors of $F_R$, $\Gamma_G$, and also of $\Gamma_X$. Choose any resolution $M\to I$. Its computation units are invertible on $I$; since $C(F_R)I$ is K-injective by Step 3, the intermediate computation unit for $\Gamma_G$ is invertible there too. Consequently $C(F_R)I$ and $C(\Gamma_G)C(F_R)I$ are exactly the claimed representatives.

proof.text: Naturality of $\gamma$ applied to each differential $d_I^n$ gives $\gamma_{I^{n+1}}\Gamma_X(d_I^n)=\operatorname{ev}_*\Gamma_GF_R(d_I^n)\gamma_{I^n}$. Thus its degreewise isomorphisms and inverses form the displayed chain isomorphism $C(\gamma)_I$. The left side computes $R\Gamma_X(M)$ by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. Exactness of $\operatorname{ev}_*$ from Step 1 permits termwise localization by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], so the right side represents $D(\operatorname{ev}_*)(R\Gamma_G)(RF_R)(M)$. No K-injective-preservation claim for singleton evaluation is needed.

source.place: Tags 070Y and 015F, K-injective computation and exact postcomposition; the differential identity is naturality

proof.text: For resolutions $i:M\to I$, $j:N\to J$ and $h:QM\to QN$, [lem-sf-kinjective-derived-map-computation] gives the unique homotopy class $t:I\to J$ with $Qt=(Qj)h(Qi)^{-1}$; every derived-functor map in these resolution coordinates is obtained by applying the corresponding additive functor to $t$. Apply this also at the intermediate K-injectives $F_RI,F_RJ$. Naturality of $\gamma$ gives the equality of chain maps $\operatorname{ev}_*\Gamma_GF_R(t)\,C(\gamma)_I=C(\gamma)_J\,\Gamma_X(t)$. Its localized equality is precisely naturality of the comparison on $h$. Taking $h=1$ proves compatibility with canonical changes of resolution; the cocycle identity for those changes is supplied by the same cited computation statement.

source.place: Tag 070Y and the arbitrary-resolution computation of the cited node; chain naturality square

proof.text: Put $L=a^*E_R^{-1}$. Apply [lem-sfb-derived-composition-adjunction-normalization] with $(\mathcal A,\mathcal B,\mathcal C)=(\mathcal M_R,\mathcal A_G(R),\operatorname{Mod}_{R_X})$, $L_a=T_G$, $L_b=L$, $L_c=LT_G$, and right adjoints $R_a=\Gamma_G$, $R_b=F_R$, $R_c=\Gamma_GF_R$, the last endowed with the composite adjunction. Take $\lambda$ to be the identity compositor. All left adjoints are exact by Step 3. The conjugate $\kappa$ is the identity and the cited theorem identifies the derived composition with the identity on $C(\Gamma_G)C(F_R)I$, with exactly the composite units and counits. Step 2 identified the underived section comparison with the normalized restriction/equalizer comparison for the specified geometric adjunction, so after exact singleton evaluation its chain representative is $C(\gamma)_I$. Step 6 then identifies its class on every resolution with the canonical comparison. Every input used applies to unbounded complexes; none imposes a cohomological-dimension bound on $G$.
